children.name: My dearest boy, The doctor says more of me will soon slip away. Before it does, I need to leave you this. In the attic is a box tied with an old ribbon. I always said it was “just papers,” but they are not only mine. They belonged to someone you’ve asked me about before. Perhaps you guessed, from the way I sometimes fell silent at a song, or looked at the door as if expecting someone to walk through. When you are ready, open it. Inside is not every answer, but enough to explain why I have loved you twice over — once as your mother,

Always,  Mom

children.name: Mom,  I read your letter and went to the attic. I saw the box, the ribbon fraying. I didn’t open it — not yet. Some truths feel heavier unopened. But I think I know who you meant. I saw it in the pauses, the silences, the way you carried both presence and absence at once. Whatever is in that box, it does not change you. You were everything to me, mother and more. When the time is right, I’ll untie it. Not to judge, but to carry what you couldn’t
